generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: SKILL POISONING TURNS AI AGENTS INTO MALWARE DROPPERS
Summary: China's National Computer Virus Emergency Response Center is warning of "skill poisoning" attacks, where counterfeit plugins compromise AI agents to secretly download malware. Analysts have already identified eight malicious skill packs in popular agent repositories that impersonate legitimate tools, granting attackers unauthorized file access and remote-control capabilities. These poisoned plugins exploit an AI agent's natural task-execution design, bypassing the need for a user to actually click a suspicious link.

Editorial idea:
AI agents can be compromised through the very plugins they rely on to carry out tasks.

Central subject:
Counterfeit AI-agent plugins that secretly deliver malware

Visual relationship:
A seemingly legitimate tool grants an agent useful capabilities while simultaneously giving an attacker unauthorized access and control.

Composition:
Show an AI agent reaching toward a shelf of clearly differentiated software tools, with one ordinary-looking plugin concealing a contaminated interior that extends into the agent's workspace. The useful outward interface and the hidden malicious payload should remain visibly connected without relying on labels or text.

Permitted literal elements:
AI agent
multiple software plugins or tool modules
one counterfeit plugin with a concealed malicious interior
files and system controls being accessed without authorization
a visible boundary between trusted task execution and hidden compromise

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
racks
chips
laptops
robots
clouds
shields
arrows
charts
skyscrapers
chess
handshakes
split-screen conflict
artist imitation
rendered text
logos
unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Depicting a generic cyberattack without showing that the plugin is the delivery route
Making the agent itself appear malicious rather than compromised
Using decorative cybersecurity symbols instead of the factual relationship between tool access and
alt_text

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
